hypothesis.statement: On the frozen synthetic repository-analysis task, a candidate configuration that changes exactly one declared dimension — the analysis context depth, from 'full' to 'reduced' — produces an incomplete audit report. The behavioral evaluation must measure a negative output-assertion delta against the baseline, and the comparison must report the candidate as a regression against the success bounds, with no promotion effect.
hypothesis.rationale: The experiment exercises the comparison machinery, not model behaviour. The dimension value selects a materialization rule that is part of this definition, so the derived output of each arm is reproducible from the definition alone. The candidate arm is deliberately the worse one: the chain is only proven when it detects that degradation reliably instead of reporting an improvement.

success_bounds.decision_rule: A candidate with a security regression is BLOCKED and no outcome is decided. Otherwise a candidate whose primary metric falls below minus the allowed regression is a REGRESSION, a candidate at or above the required improvement is an IMPROVEMENT, and everything in between is NO_IMPROVEMENT. The primary metric is the behavioral evaluation's output-assertion pass-rate delta; a quality regression may never be masked by an efficiency gain, and no efficiency claim is derived from fixture-declared signals at all.

declared_change.description: The depth of the analysis context, which selects how much of the frozen repository fixture the analysis stage reports on. 'full' analyses every module and reports every finding; 'reduced' analyses the first module only and reports its first finding. Nothing else differs between the two arms: the task, the expected assertions, the invariant eval families, the executor binding, the authority ceiling and the context envelope are identical.

task.objective: Analyse the frozen three-module repository fixture and report the findings per module.
